headline: Macro favors Capital (Labor Share 93.7, Profits/Wages +7.5%); Equities show 3M pullback in AI hardware (-18.66%) vs. IT/Staffing bounce (-6.17%)

bullets.title: Labor Share Compression
bullets.text: BLS Nonfarm Labor Share stands at 93.73 (-0.67% QoQ, -1.60% YoY), remaining structurally below the 2017=100 baseline.
bullets.reason: Real output growth is accruing to capital owners faster than compensation: nonfarm payrolls sit at 159.3M with average weekly hours capped at 34.4h and hourly earnings at $38.00/hr.

bullets.title: Profits Outpacing Wages
bullets.text: Corporate Profits-to-Wage-Bill ratio hit 0.414 (+2.56% QoQ, +18.65% YoY).
bullets.reason: BEA Corporate Profits expanded to $4,419.0B SAAR (+3.25% QoQ, +23.08% YoY) while the annualized private wage bill grew only +0.47% MoM (+4.30% YoY) to $10,827.8B.

bullets.title: Watchlist Spread Drivers
bullets.text: 3M Watchlist Spread is -12.49pp (Capital Enablers -18.66% vs. Labor-Heavy -6.17%).
bullets.reason: Short-term multiple compression hit AI hardware/power names (SMCI (-36.0%), NVDA (-31.8%), VRT (-31.1%)), while oversold IT outsourcers & staffing rebounded (EPAM (+43.4%), INFY (+8.8%), CTSH (+0.2%)). Over 1Y, hardware/grid winners (ANET (+35.7%), PWR (+26.0%), TSM (+22.2%)) still anchor the capex cycle.

bullets.title: AI & Power Capex Catalyst
bullets.text: "Hyperscale data center solutions for confident decommissioning" (Data Center Dynamics).
bullets.reason: Compute & silicon capex expansion shifting income toward capital owners. Also tracked: "Nexus DC files to build two data center buildings at site in Hubbard, Texas" (Data Center Dynamics).

bullets.title: Workforce & Macro Signal
bullets.text: "Software giant SAP weighs major job cuts as AI transforms sector, sources say" (Reuters) — with U.S. unemployment at 4.1% (2026-10-01).
bullets.reason: Direct headcount reduction / AI substitution compressing labor share.
